classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied volume and surface-area scaffolding, differentiate to establish a global minimum, and substitute to show that height equals diameter.

content.prompt: A certain cylindrical soft drink can is required to have a volume of $250\text{ cm}^3$.

spec.sourceRegion: Cylinder below question 20 on the left
spec.description: Upright closed cylinder with an elliptical top, visible curved lower rim, a centre-to-right-rim radius arrow labelled r and an external vertical height arrow labelled h. Non-mathematical grey shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Closed cylinder of radius r and height h; no numerical dimensions are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied figure; no solution information.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the height of the can is $\frac{250}{\pi r^2}$, where $r$ is the base radius.

answer.worked:
Let the height of the can be $h$ cm. The volume is $\pi r^2h$.
$$\begin{align*}250&=\pi r^2h\\h&=\frac{250}{\pi r^2}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the total surface area is $S=2\pi r^2+\frac{500}{r}$.

answer.worked:
Each end has area $\pi r^2$ and the curved side has area $2\pi rh$.
$$\begin{align*}S&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\S&=2\pi r^2+2\pi r\times\frac{250}{\pi r^2}\\S&=2\pi r^2+\frac{500}{r},\qquad r>0.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that $r=\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}$ gives a global minimum of $S$ in the domain $r>0$.

answer.short: $r=\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}$ is stationary and $\frac{d^2S}{dr^2}=4\pi+\frac{1000}{r^3}>0$ for every $r>0$, so it gives the global minimum.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dS}{dr}&=4\pi r-\frac{500}{r^2}\\\frac{dS}{dr}&=\frac{4\pi r^3-500}{r^2}.\end{align*}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dS}{dr}&=0\\4\pi r^3&=500\\r^3&=\frac{125}{\pi}\\r&=\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}.\end{align*}$$
Also,
$$\frac{d^2S}{dr^2}=4\pi+\frac{1000}{r^3}>0\qquad\text{for all }r>0.$$
Thus the derivative is strictly increasing throughout the domain, and the stationary point gives a global minimum.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Show that to minimise the can’s surface area, the base diameter should equal its height.

answer.short: $h=\frac{10}{\pi^{1/3}}=2r$, so the height equals the base diameter.
answer.worked:
When $r=\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}$,
$$\begin{align*}h&=\frac{250}{\pi r^2}\\h&=\frac{250}{\pi\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{\pi}}\right)^2}\\h&=\frac{250}{\pi\left(\frac{25}{\pi^{2/3}}\right)}\\h&=\frac{10}{\pi^{1/3}}\\h&=2r.\end{align*}$$
Hence the minimum surface area occurs when the base diameter equals the height.
